answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by binding each identity to a unique hardware nadir whose resonance must match a living harbor of attested devices; any mismatch drops the claim into a quarantine lotus. Verification requires the device to solve a fresh challenge rooted in its physical properties, so an attacker forging k clones must procure k distinct unclonable modules and keep them online for continuous re-checks. This imposes a linear procurement cost plus ongoing power and custody overhead that cannot be shared across aliases, while a single honest agent pays the cost once.
